open_release.rationale: The paper and README frame the synthetic notes and models as publicly shareable substitutes for private clinical notes.

quotes.text: All resources including weights, codes, and data used in the development of Asclepius are made publicly accessible for future research.
The model checkpoints and data are publicly available via huggingface.

pipeline_testing.rationale: The synthetic notes are built to train a clinical LLM, not to exercise software or formats.

ml_augmentation.rationale: The synthetic notes are the training data for the Asclepius LLM, which is then evaluated on real notes.

quotes.text: we trained our model, **Asclepius**, on synthetic clinical notes generated from publicly available case reports extracted from biomedical literature.
Our findings convincingly demonstrate that synthetic clinical notes can serve as viable substitutes for real ones when constructing high-performing clinical language models.

statistical_replication.rationale: Evaluation is of downstream LLM answers (GPT-4 and clinicians), not distributional fidelity of the synthetic notes to real notes.

causal_inference.rationale: No causal structure or intervention framing appears in the sources.

education.rationale: The only mention of education refers to the source case reports, not to the synthetic notes being teaching material.

benchmarking.rationale: The paper benchmarks the trained LLM against other LLMs, but does not present the generator or synthetic notes as a baseline or benchmark for generators.

imbalance_correction.rationale: No class-imbalance or minority-class framing appears in the sources.
